ADA Transition Plan Comment Card
Name Justin Foell
Email justin@foell.org
Comments Two issues I'd like to submit for the record: 1. Curb extensions or "Bumpouts" for
pedestrian safety and speed of crossing. 2. Our obligation to influence county and
state agencies. When talking about ADA compliance for road crossing time, the
Federal Highway Administration simply want to make sure users have enough time to
complete their crossing "the distance from the curb to the far side of the opposing
travel way, or to a median of sufficient width for pedestrians to wait." While they don't
reference adjusting the distance to be traveled, minimizing the pedestrian distance
should be our goal. There are studies that show how reducing the crossing distance
helps for pedestrian safety. This one is widely cited:
https://nacto.org/docs/usdg/pedestrian_safety_impacts_of_curb_extensions_randal.pdf
Here's a Minnesota example using just paint and planters:
http://www.mikeontraffic.com/temporary-bumpouts-with-paint-coming-to-pine-island-
mn/ A couple of intersections that could use this treatment come to mind: 61st & West
Moore Lake Drive - turning right from the shoulder lane is already prohibited Other
spots along 61st near: Fridley High and Middle School Fridley Community Center (how
was this not in the Fridley ADA Transition Document List?!?) 73rd & Madsen Park /
Grace Church - it would be nice to have 73rd neck-down to 2-lanes and have a
crossing where the bike path exits Melody Manor Park, across 73rd to Madsen Park.
The speed limit would not need to be changed, just reduce the lanes for the crossing
to provide a shorter distance to cross traffic. This could easily be tested with bollards
and planters without doing anything permanent. Secondly, I want to stress that it is
Fridley's responsibility to influence the larger political entities who "own" right-of-ways
in our community. Many of these we already maintain - so we see first hand what the
design and use issues are. In the Anoka County ADA plan it states that "ADA
improvements requested by the public will be evaluated by County staff. Evaluation
criteria will include pedestrian volumes, traffic volumes, condition of existing
infrastructure and public safety." Fridley city residents, staff, the mayor,
councilpersons, and commissioners *must* be that voice to the county and the state
(MnDOT). We know our town better than they do, and we know what issues people
encounter on a day-to-day basis, even if they're the entity responsible for a particular
right-of-way.
